code_snippet:
sgit add -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
sgit commit -q --allow-empty -m "snapshot $label" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
reasoning_trace: Traced the post-phase snapshot path: sgit (pipeline-run.sh:446-449) runs host-side git -C $WS with env -i GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1; $WS/.git is inside the /workspace rw bind mount the agent owns (:689). Repo-local hooks and config are not covered by those variables. Reproduced on git 2.39.5: a planted .git/hooks/pre-commit and a core.fsmonitor command both executed under the exact sgit environment on git add -A / git commit --allow-empty. The same PR pins core.hooksPath for hermetic git in tools/fresh-mount-proof.sh:96, so the author knows the class.
finding: Host-side git on an agent-writable .git executes sandbox-planted hooks and config commands on the host as the operator, defeating the container boundary.
critique: The container flags (--read-only, --pids-limit, --memory, two mounts) contain the agent only while the host never executes anything under its control; git on the sandbox .git breaks that assumption.
remediation: Keep the snapshot repo outside the mount: git --git-dir="$META/snap.git" --work-tree="$WS" for init/base/add/commit/bundle; or pass -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c commit.gpgsign=false on every sgit call. Add a bats case that plants a pre-commit hook and asserts it did not run.

reasoning_trace: Review §1 re-verified: jq-1.6 on this host rejects `$label` as a binding and `{label}` shorthand (syntax error, unexpected label). Same construct at pipeline-run.sh:816, :881, lib/sandbox-mount.sh:462-467, ablation-row.sh:285. Under set -e the argv capture aborts run_phase before any phase; write_sandbox_grimoire returns 2; ablation-row.sh exits 3. CI runs ubuntu-latest (jq 1.7) and cannot see it; Dockerfile.ablation:22 pins a bookworm base whose jq is 1.6.
finding: jq keyword `label` used as a variable binding and object shorthand; every pipeline run and every row build fails on jq 1.6.
critique: No jq minimum is declared and the repository's existing scripts avoid the construct.
remediation: Rename the binding to lbl at pipeline-run.sh:702,816,881 and sandbox-mount.sh:462; expand ablation-row.sh:285 to label: .label; add an ubuntu-22.04 CI leg.
references: jq 1.7 changelog: keywords as binding names

reasoning_trace: Review §2 and dissent DISS-C-003 re-verified by reading the path: ACTUAL_COUNT is an index count; a working-tree deletion of a tracked file or a planted untracked file leaves it unchanged; the pre-PR find count (now only the zero-count fallback at :195-197) detected both. The manifest is generated from git ls-files too (tools/gen-checksums.sh:102), so the comparison is tautological for on-disk changes. In strict mode this is the only pre-operation fence.
finding: System Zone file-count fence no longer detects deleted tracked files or planted untracked files.
critique: Counting the index against a manifest derived from the index detects nothing a tamper on disk would cause.
remediation: Filter tracked paths through [[ -f ]] and add git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- .claude, or verify sha256; add bats cases for a deleted and a planted file.

reasoning_trace: Review §3 and dissent DISS-C-001 re-verified: every linked path exists under .loa/ by construction in a submodule mount; mount-submodule.sh logs Linked lines (:908-965) but persists no link set, so a removed link is indistinguishable from a never-linked path and is reported as informational not-mounted with exit 0.
finding: In a submodule mount, deleting any linked .claude/ file is reported as not-mounted (informational) instead of Missing (fail).
critique: An integrity check that cannot fail on deletion is not an integrity check for that mount mode.
remediation: Persist the linked set at mount time and classify absent linked paths as Missing; print not-mounted paths; add a bats case that removes a linked file.

code_snippet: for f in auth.json config.toml; do if [[ -f "$CREDS_HOME/.codex/$f" ]]; then cp "$CREDS_HOME/.codex/$f" "$HOME_DIR/.codex/$f"; fi; done
reasoning_trace: make_home copies the operator's codex OAuth token file into <run>/meta/home, bind-mounted rw into the container. remove_tree runs only in finish and the EXIT trap (:348, :356). The header (:105-106) explicitly plans for a SIGKILLed driver, in which case the token copy persists in the run directory that the batch tooling archives.
finding: Operator credential copies in the run directory outlive the run when the driver is killed.
critique: A per-run HOME inside the archived run tree couples credential lifetime to a trap that SIGKILL never fires.
remediation: Create the per-run HOME under mktemp -d outside the run tree; sweep meta/home of status:running runs at batch start.

reasoning_trace: Review Observation 4 confirmed: 137 before timeout is interrupted; a container OOM-kill under --memory 4g (:688) is also 137 and the suite excludes interrupted rows (ablation-2.0.yaml:83); docker client exit 125 reaches :862 as agent_error.
finding: OOM-kills are excluded as interrupted and docker-client failures are charged as agent errors.
critique: The pre-registered exclusion rules depend on the status taxonomy being honest.
remediation: Inspect .State.OOMKilled via --cidfile; map OOM to agent_error/cap_failure and 125 to infrastructure_error.
